Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১) Which is an acute complication of diabetes mellitus?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Lactic acidosis is an acute metabolic complication associated with diabetes mellitus, particularly in settings such as severe tissue hypoxia or metformin-associated lactic acidosis. In contrast, diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, and peripheral vascular disease are chronic complications of diabetes.

High-yield Acute complications of diabetes recall:

  • Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)

  • Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS)

  • Hypoglycemia

  • Lactic acidosis

Exam pearl: Acute = DKA, HHS, hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis; chronic = retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, macrovascular disease.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ২) Which is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Graves' disease is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism, especially in younger adults. It is an autoimmune disorder caused by thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) that stimulate the TSH receptor, resulting in excessive production of T3 and T4.

High-yield Graves' disease recall:

  • Most common cause of hyperthyroidism

  • Autoimmune disease

  • TSH receptor antibody/TSI positive

  • Diffuse goiter

  • May cause ophthalmopathy and pretibial myxedema

Exam pearl: Young patient + diffuse toxic goiter + eye signs = Graves' disease.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৩) Which one is a feature of Type-1 DM?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.option2: history of other autoimmune disease common
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is an autoimmune disease caused by destruction of pancreatic β-cells, leading to absolute insulin deficiency. Therefore, it is commonly associated with other autoimmune disorders such as autoimmune thyroid disease, coeliac disease, and Addison's disease.

The other options are more characteristic of Type 2 DM: family history is stronger, obesity is common, and onset typically occurs in adulthood.

High-yield Type 1 DM recall:

  • Autoimmune β-cell destruction

  • Absolute insulin deficiency

  • Other autoimmune diseases commonly associated

  • Usually younger onset

  • Usually lean, though obesity can occur

  • Requires insulin therapy

Exam pearl: Type 1 DM = autoimmune + β-cell destruction + absolute insulin deficiency.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৪) Which drug is safe to be used in hyperthyroidism with pregnancy?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: PTU is preferred during the first trimester of pregnancy because carbimazole/methimazole carries a risk of congenital malformations, particularly when used in early pregnancy. After the first trimester, carbimazole/methimazole is generally preferred because prolonged PTU use carries a risk of hepatotoxicity. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated throughout pregnancy because it can destroy the fetal thyroid.

High-yield Hyperthyroidism in pregnancy recall:

  • 1st trimester: PTU preferred

  • After 1st trimester: Carbimazole/methimazole preferred

  • Radioactive iodine: Contraindicated

  • Use the lowest effective antithyroid drug dose to maintain maternal euthyroidism.

Exam pearl: Pregnancy + 1st trimester + hyperthyroidism = PTU.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৫) The risk of developing type-2 DM increases......... in a people with a BMI > 30 kg/m2 ?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: A BMI >30 kg/m² (obesity) markedly increases the risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus. Classically, obesity is associated with approximately a 10-fold increased risk compared with people with normal BMI.

High-yield Type 2 DM risk factors recall:

  • Obesity, particularly central obesity

  • Physical inactivity

  • Family history of type 2 DM

  • Increasing age

  • History of gestational diabetes

  • Hypertension and dyslipidemia

Exam pearl: BMI >30 kg/m² → approximately 10-fold increased risk of type 2 DM.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৬) Which one is pathophysiology of Type-1 DM?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.option4: elevated plasma glucose & free fatty acids
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Insulitis is the characteristic pathological process in Type 1 diabetes mellitus, involving autoimmune-mediated inflammation and destruction of pancreatic β-cells. This ultimately causes absolute insulin deficiency.

  • Insulin resistance → mainly characteristic of Type 2 DM.

  • β-cell failure → occurs prominently in Type 2 DM as the disease progresses.

  • Elevated plasma glucose and free fatty acids → metabolic consequences rather than the primary pathological mechanism of Type 1 DM.

High-yield Type 1 DM pathophysiology recall:
Autoimmune β-cell destruction → insulitis → progressive loss of β-cells → absolute insulin deficiency → hyperglycemia.

Exam pearl: Type 1 DM = autoimmune β-cell destruction; the histopathological hallmark is insulitis.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৭) Which is a contraindication of subtotal thyroidectomy in a hyperthyroid patient?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: A patient who is highly dependent on their voice (e.g., professional singer, public speaker, teacher) is a relative contraindication to thyroidectomy because recurrent laryngeal nerve injury can cause vocal cord paralysis and permanent voice changes. In such patients, non-surgical treatment may be preferred when appropriate.

High-yield Thyroidectomy contraindications recall:

  • Voice-dependent profession → important relative contraindication

  • Unfit for anesthesia → contraindication to surgery

  • Large goiter, poor compliance with antithyroid drugs, and recurrent thyrotoxicosis → may actually be indications for surgery

Exam pearl: Hyperthyroidism + professional voice user → avoid thyroidectomy if a suitable alternative exists.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৮) What is the significance of following blood glucose level? FBS : 6.1-6.9 mmol/L & 2hrs ABF : <7.8 mmol/L
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: FBS 6.1–6.9 mmol/L indicates impaired fasting glucose (IFG) according to the classic WHO diagnostic criteria. The 2-hour postprandial glucose <7.8 mmol/L is within the normal range, so this pattern is classified as IFG rather than IGT or diabetes mellitus.

High-yield Prediabetes recall:

  • IFG: Fasting plasma glucose 6.1–6.9 mmol/L (WHO criterion)

  • IGT: 2-hour OGTT glucose 7.8–11.0 mmol/L

  • Diabetes mellitus: Fasting plasma glucose ≥7.0 mmol/L or 2-hour OGTT ≥11.1 mmol/L

Exam pearl: Raised fasting glucose with normal 2-hour glucose = IFG.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ৯) What is the target BP of a diabetic patient without proteinuria?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: In a patient with diabetes mellitus without proteinuria, the commonly taught target blood pressure is <130/80 mmHg. Tight BP control reduces the risk of diabetic nephropathy, retinopathy, and cardiovascular complications.

High-yield Diabetes + hypertension recall:

  • Diabetes without proteinuria → target <130/80 mmHg

  • Diabetes with significant albuminuria/proteinuria → ACE inhibitor or ARB is particularly useful for renal protection.

  • BP control is an important component of preventing diabetic microvascular complications.

Exam pearl: Diabetes + no proteinuria → BP target <130/80 mmHg.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১০) Which oral antidiabetic drug is biguanides?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Metformin is a biguanide and is generally considered the first-line pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly in patients who are overweight or obese. It primarily reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis and improves insulin sensitivity.

High-yield Oral antidiabetic drugs recall:

  • Biguanide: Metformin

  • Sulfonylurea: Glimepiride

  • Thiazolidinedione (TZD): Rosiglitazone

  • DPP-4 inhibitor: Sitagliptin

Exam pearl: Metformin = Biguanide = ↓ hepatic glucose production.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১১) Which jerk is affected in hypothyroidism?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Hypothyroidism classically causes delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes, most characteristically seen in the ankle jerk (Achilles reflex). This is due to delayed calcium reuptake and prolonged muscle relaxation.

In contrast, hyperthyroidism tends to cause brisk/exaggerated reflexes.

High-yield Hypothyroidism recall:

  • Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes

  • Ankle jerk is classically affected

  • Other features: bradycardia, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin

Exam pearl: Hypothyroidism → delayed ankle jerk relaxation; hyperthyroidism → brisk reflexes.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১২) Which insulin preparation is rapid acting?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Insulin aspart is a rapid-acting insulin analogue with a quick onset and short duration of action. It is commonly administered immediately before meals to control postprandial blood glucose.

  • Isophane (NPH) → intermediate-acting

  • Ultralente → long-acting

  • Glargine → long-acting, relatively peakless insulin

High-yield Insulin preparation recall:

  • Rapid-acting: Lispro, Aspart, Glulisine

  • Short-acting: Regular insulin

  • Intermediate-acting: NPH (Isophane)

  • Long-acting: Glargine, Detemir, Degludec

Exam pearl: Rapid-acting insulin analogues = Lispro, Aspart, Glulisine.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৩) Which is not true about metformin?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.option4: useful in prevention of type-2 DM
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
weight loss, so the statement that it increases body weight is false. It improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis. As monotherapy, it has a very low risk of hypoglycemia and is also used to reduce the progression from prediabetes to type 2 DM in selected high-risk patients.

High-yield Metformin recall:

  • Weight: Neutral or ↓

  • Hypoglycemia: Rare when used alone

  • Action: ↓ hepatic gluconeogenesis + ↑ insulin sensitivity

  • Insulin-sparing: Yes

  • Prevention of type 2 DM: Can reduce progression in high-risk prediabetes

Exam pearl: Metformin = weight-neutral/weight loss + minimal hypoglycemia + ↓ hepatic glucose production.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৪) Which is the ECG finding of hypothyroidism?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Low-voltage ECG is a recognized ECG finding in hypothyroidism, mainly due to reduced myocardial activity and sometimes pericardial effusion. Other possible findings include sinus bradycardia, prolonged QT interval, and nonspecific ST-T changes.

  • Sinus tachycardia → more consistent with hyperthyroidism.

  • ST elevation → not a typical finding of hypothyroidism.

  • Tall T waves → classically associated with hyperkalemia.

High-yield Hypothyroidism ECG recall:

  • Low-voltage QRS

  • Sinus bradycardia

  • Prolonged QT interval

  • Nonspecific ST-T changes

  • Pericardial effusion may contribute to low voltage

Exam pearl: Hypothyroidism → low voltage + bradycardia + prolonged QT.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৫) Which is not a cardinal biochemical features of DKA?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: The cardinal biochemical features of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) are hyperglycemia, hyperketonemia/ketonuria, and metabolic acidosis. Therefore, metabolic alkalosis is not a cardinal feature.

DKA develops due to severe insulin deficiency with increased counter-regulatory hormones, causing increased lipolysis and ketone-body production. Accumulation of ketones produces a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

High-yield DKA biochemical features recall:

  • Hyperglycemia

  • Hyperketonemia/ketonuria

  • High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis

  • Low serum bicarbonate

  • Usually low or normal pH

Exam pearl: DKA = Hyperglycemia + Ketosis + Metabolic acidosis.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৬) What is the single most important investigation in hypothyroidism?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: Serum TSH is the single most important initial investigation for suspected primary hypothyroidism. In primary hypothyroidism, reduced thyroid hormone production causes loss of negative feedback, resulting in elevated TSH. FT4 is then used to confirm and assess the severity.

High-yield Hypothyroidism investigation recall:

  • Primary hypothyroidism: ↑ TSH, ↓ FT4

  • Subclinical hypothyroidism: ↑ TSH, normal FT4

  • Secondary hypothyroidism: ↓/inappropriately normal TSH, ↓ FT4

  • Thyroid scan is not routinely required for diagnosis.

Exam pearl: Suspected primary hypothyroidism → check serum TSH first.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৭) What is the average amount of water loss in an adult patient of DKA with moderate severity?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: In moderate-severity DKA, the average water deficit in an adult is approximately 6 litres. Severe insulin deficiency causes marked hyperglycemia, leading to osmotic diuresis, which results in substantial loss of water along with sodium, potassium, and other electrolytes.

High-yield DKA fluid deficit recall:

  • Moderate DKA → approximately 6 L water deficit in an adult

  • Major mechanism → osmotic diuresis due to hyperglycemia

  • Fluid replacement is a key initial component of DKA management.

Exam pearl: Moderate DKA in an adult → remember approximately 6 L water loss.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৮) Clinical triad of Grave's disease excludes......?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Explanation: The classic clinical triad of Graves' disease consists of goiter, exophthalmos (ophthalmopathy), and pretibial myxedema. Therefore, tremor is not part of the classic triad, although it is a common clinical feature of thyrotoxicosis.

High-yield Graves' disease recall:

  • Goiter → diffuse, usually vascular

  • Exophthalmos → Graves' ophthalmopathy

  • Pretibial myxedema → infiltrative dermopathy

  • Tremor → common symptom of hyperthyroidism, but not part of the classic triad

Exam pearl: Graves' triad = Goiter + Exophthalmos + Pretibial myxedema.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ১৯) Which is the feature of hypoglycemic coma?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Hypoglycemic coma is caused by severe neuroglycopenia and activation of the sympathoadrenal system. This produces adrenergic features, including sweating, tremor, tachycardia, and a bounding pulse.

  • Abdominal pain → more suggestive of DKA.

  • Blurring of vision → may occur with hypoglycemia but is not the characteristic finding asked here.

  • Features of shock → not a typical primary feature of hypoglycemic coma.

High-yield Hypoglycemia recall:

  • Adrenergic: sweating, tremor, palpitations, bounding pulse, anxiety

  • Neuroglycopenic: confusion, abnormal behavior, seizures, coma

  • Severe hypoglycemia → loss of consciousness/coma

Exam pearl: Hypoglycemia → adrenergic activation → sweating + tremor + tachycardia + bounding pulse.

Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.question: ২০) Which is a feature of autonomic neuropathy in diabetic patient?
Diabetes mellitus, Thyrotoxicosis, Hypot.exp:
Gustatory sweating is a characteristic manifestation of diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Patients develop excessive sweating over the face and neck while eating, particularly with spicy or certain foods, due to abnormal sympathetic nerve activity.

The other options are manifestations of diabetic peripheral/focal neuropathies:

  • Ocular palsies → diabetic cranial mononeuropathy

  • Amyotrophy → diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy

  • Carpal tunnel syndrome → diabetic entrapment neuropathy

High-yield Diabetic autonomic neuropathy recall:

  • Gustatory sweating

  • Postural hypotension

  • Resting tachycardia

  • Gastroparesis

  • Bladder dysfunction

  • Erectile dysfunction

  • Hypoglycemia unawareness

Exam pearl: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy + sweating while eating = gustatory sweating.
